record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Is every torsion-free Engel group right-orderable?

evidence.quote: 2.9. Is every torsion-free Engel group right orderable? (cf. Problems 1.12, 2.8, 2.25, 2.29, 3.4, 3.8, 3.9, 3.18)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called an Engel group if for every pair of elements $x, y \in G$ there exists a non-negative integer $n = n(x,y)$ such that the iterated commutator
$$[x, \underbrace{y, y, \dots, y}_{n}] = 1,$$
where $[a,b] = a^{-1}b^{-1}ab$ and $[x, y, \dots, y] = [[x, y, \dots, y], y]$ is defined recursively. The group $G$ is torsion-free if it has no non-identity element of finite order. A group $G$ is right-orderable if there exists a total order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a,b,c \in G$.

Question: Is every torsion-free Engel group right-orderable?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. Related results are known: bi-orderable Engel groups are nilpotent (Kim–Rhemtulla), and an orderable n-Engel group is nilpotent. The closely related question of whether every torsion-free k-Engel group is orderable also remains open and appears as a problem in the Kourovka Notebook. No source found establishes right-orderability of all torsion-free Engel groups.
